extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, program committee members, and researchers developing paper–reviewer matching systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating automated systems that suggest assignments of submitted papers to qualified reviewers for large academic conferences, while satisfying operational constraints. Focus is on scalability, assignment quality, and integration with conference-management tooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability for large conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Large conferences typically have to assign hundreds of papers to hundreds of reviewers, and time constraints make the task impossible for one person to accomplish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should be able to handle assignment at the scale of major conferences (hundreds of papers/reviewers) and operate under tight time constraints; automation is required rather than manual assignment by a single organizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect reviewer load constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Other constraints, such as reviewer load have to be taken into account, preventing the process from being completely distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment algorithms must enforce constraints on per-reviewer load and other operational limits (e.g., maximum number of papers per reviewer) so the assignment is feasible and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce high-quality reviewer-paper matches (assignment quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' assessments of papers is a crucial step in determining the conference program, and in a certain sense to shape the direction of a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching should prioritize expertise/alignment so that reviewer assessments are informative; assignment quality directly affects program selection and the field's trajectory, so objective measures of match quality should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated suggestion capability
rubrics_metrics.description: We built the first version of a system to suggest reviewer assignments for the NIPS 2010 conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system should generate recommended assignments (not necessarily final decisions) to assist organizers and PC chairs, reducing manual workload while allowing human oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with conference management tools
rubrics_metrics.description: A release that better integrated our system with Microsoft's popular Conference Management Toolkit (CMT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical deployment requires integration with existing conference-management platforms (e.g., CMT) to fit into organizers' workflows; interoperability and export/import formats are important considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of learning models and systematic evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of learning models and methods of evaluation that we have been using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and selection of matching approaches should be grounded in machine-learning models and validated with explicit evaluation methods/metrics; papers/systems should report these models and their evaluation protocols and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and report open issues and ongoing progress
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper provides an overview of the system, a summary of learning models and methods of evaluation that we have been using, as well as some of the recent progress and open issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors/developers should acknowledge limitations and open challenges of the matching approach and report recent improvements to guide future work and adoption.
